A.why: Uses the bone palette and a striking spire, but reads as a pale stone column with broad shoulders, not a flaring gown.

B.why: Clear flared skirt and gothic plume hat, but the skirt splays into separate wedges with gaps and the black bodice is wide and heavy.

C.why: A-line front skirt and fern crown read as a dress head-on, but blocky wide sleeves and a column back weaken it from above.

D.why: Tiered ruffled bell skirt and mushroom-cap hat nail the fungal forest-lady idea; wide dark sleeves and an uncinched waist hold it back.

E.why: Tiered front skirt and mushroom-button cap are nice, but a near-black boxy top and a column back read as a coat from above.

F.why: Fern crest and lichen patches carry the theme, but there is no skirt flare and the legs and feet read as trousers under a tunic.

notes: Every set keeps wide boxy sleeves that make the shoulders the widest point, and almost none cinch the waist; the lichen yellow-green and bone are underused, leaving most sets a murky dark green.
